system_type_reason: Hook-first runtime for building agents; every turn stage is a replaceable pluggy hook.

repo_overview.summary: Small hook-first Python runtime for agents in shared environments like CLI and Telegram group chats. Every turn stage (resolve_session, load_state, build_prompt, run_model, save_state, render_outbound, dispatch_outbound) is a pluggy hook with replaceable builtin implementations. Context is rebuilt from an append-only tape of records, and model calls go through any-llm-sdk with native tool calling.

topology.justification: One main Agent drives the step loop (agent.py:205). The model can call the subagent tool (builtin/tools.py:345-364), which starts a separate full agent loop via agent.run_stream with its own session and tape, optionally a different model and a restricted tool and skill set; only the sub-agent's text output returns to the parent. This is an orchestrator spawning dynamic sub-agents. Sub-agents share the same Agent class and system prompt, and there is no further peer communication between agents.

resilience.name: automatic context handoff on context-window overflow
resilience.what_it_is: A model-call exception whose message matches a context-length regex (context length/window, maximum context, token limit, prompt too long) triggers tape.handoff(name='auto_handoff/context_overflow'), which appends a new anchor to the tape; the step is then re-run with the original prompt. Limited to MAX_AUTO_HANDOFF_RETRIES = 1 per loop. Because the default TapeContext selects only entries after the last anchor, the rebuilt message list drops the whole prior history.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the step loop around _run_once (agent.py:234-259), catching errors raised by the model call. Recovers from context-window overflow by truncating the context at a fresh anchor and retrying the step. Otherwise an overflowing session fails every further turn with the same context-length error.

resilience.name: tool errors returned to the model as structured results
resilience.what_it_is: ToolExecutor runs all tool calls of a step via asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True). Argument validation failures (pydantic validate_call) become BubError(INVALID_INPUT) with the validation errors, any other tool exception becomes BubError(TOOL) with repr(exc); each BubError is appended as result.as_dict() to the tool results, which are recorded on the tape.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the model's tool calls and the next step (model_runner.py:113-124). Because tool_results is non-empty, the loop continues and the model sees the error in its next context, which enables self-correction. Otherwise one failing or badly-argued tool call aborts the whole turn, including the parallel calls of the same step.

resilience.name: shell command timeout with terminate-then-kill escalation
resilience.what_it_is: The bash tool waits at most timeout_seconds (default 30, adjustable by the model per call); on expiry the process gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL if it has not exited within 3 seconds, and the tool returns 'command timed out after N seconds and was terminated' as a normal result. web.fetch uses an analogous 10-second request timeout.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside tool execution within a step. Bounds the time a hanging command can block the loop, cleans up the process and reports the timeout to the model so it can react. Otherwise a hanging command stalls the turn indefinitely and leaves orphan processes.

resilience.name: context isolation via sub-agents in temporary sessions
resilience.what_it_is: The subagent tool runs a full agent loop in a session temp/<uuid> by default; tapes of temp/ sessions are forked and never merged back into the parent store. Tools can be restricted, and the subagent tool itself is always excluded for the child. Only the child's text output (with errors inlined as [Error: ...]) returns to the parent.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the tool level of the parent loop. Offloads subtasks so their intermediate steps and tool outputs stay out of the parent's context, and the self-exclusion bounds sub-agent recursion to depth one. Otherwise every exploratory step of a subtask consumes the parent's context window, and sub-agents could spawn sub-agents without limit.

resilience.name: model-initiated context handoff and tape retrieval
resilience.what_it_is: Tools let the model manage its own context: tape.handoff writes an anchor with a summary state (cutting the rebuilt context at that point), tape.reset clears the tape and, with archive=True, first writes a timestamped JSONL backup whose path is recorded in the new session/start anchor, tape.search retrieves older entries by query and date range, using substring plus rapidfuzz fuzzy matching (WRatio >= 80) with deduplication and a default limit of 20, and tape.info reports entries_since_last_anchor and last_token_usage. The default context builder renders each anchor with its state as an assistant message, so the handoff summary survives as the first message of the rebuilt context. The default system prompt contains a context_contract that instructs the model to use tape.info and tape.handoff when the context grows long.
resilience.function_in_system: Available at every step as tools. Lets the agent compact its context at phase boundaries and pull back specific past information on demand. It is the manual counterpart to the automatic overflow handoff. Otherwise context grows until it overflows, and information behind an anchor is lost to the agent.

resilience.name: on_error observer hooks per pipeline stage
resilience.what_it_is: Failures in the pipeline stages turn, run_model, resolve_session and admit_message, as well as error events from the agent stream, are dispatched via notify_error(stage=...) to all registered on_error plugin hooks; exceptions raised by the observers themselves are caught and logged so they cannot break the turn.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps the turn pipeline in framework.process_inbound and the ChannelManager. Surfaces turn failures to plugins (alerting, user notification) without changing the turn itself. The built-in on_error implementation sends the stage and error text as an error message back to the originating channel, so the user learns that the turn failed. Otherwise failures stay in the local log, the user waits for a reply that never arrives, and a faulty observer could crash error handling.

async def on_error(self, stage: str, error: Exception, message: Envelope | None) -> None:
    if message is not None:
        outbound = ChannelMessage(
            session_id=field_of(message, "session_id", "unknown"),
            channel=field_of(message, "channel", "default"),
            chat_id=field_of(message, "chat_id", "default"),
            content=f"An error occurred at stage '{stage}': {error}",
            kind="error",

resilience.name: Telegram access allowlists for users and chats
resilience.what_it_is: allow_users and allow_chats (comma-separated IDs or usernames, set via config or BUB_TELEGRAM_* env) gate every inbound Telegram message. Messages from chats outside allow_chats are dropped silently; senders outside allow_users receive 'Access denied.' and no turn is created. An empty setting means no restriction.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the Telegram channel entry, before debounce, turn admission and the agent loop. Restricts who can trigger model calls and tool execution, including the bash tool, on the operator's instance. Otherwise anyone who finds the bot can start turns at the operator's expense and have shell commands run in the workspace.

resilience.name: on-demand skill expansion (progressive disclosure)
resilience.what_it_is: The system prompt lists every discovered skill as a single '- name: description' line. render_skills_prompt appends the location and full SKILL.md body only for skills referenced as $name in the prompt (HINT_RE); any other skill body is loaded on demand through the skill(name) tool.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs in the system-prompt construction of every step. Keeps the per-skill prompt cost to one line and brings skill bodies into context only when a skill is actually needed. The docs separate the description the agent reads when listing skills from the body it loads when a skill is expanded. Otherwise the full text of every installed skill is sent with every model call, which costs thousands of tokens per step as the number of skills grows.

resilience.name: proactive failure reporting policy in the Telegram skill
resilience.what_it_is: The Active Response Policy of the built-in telegram skill instructs the agent to send an immediate acknowledgment, progress updates via message edits, and, when execution is blocked or fails, an immediate problem report with cause, impact and next action.
resilience.function_in_system: Acts through the agent's outbound messages while a Telegram turn runs. Surfaces failures that happen inside the turn to the user, complementing the on_error hooks that cover pipeline failures. Otherwise the Telegram user waits for a reply to a task that has already failed, because the agent's direct reply is discarded for Telegram messages (output_channel="null").

evidence.snippet:
## Active Response Policy

When this skill is in scope, prefer proactive and timely Telegram updates:

- Send an immediate acknowledgment for newly assigned tasks
- Send progress updates for long-running operations using message edits
- Send completion notifications when work finishes
- Send important status or failure notifications without waiting for follow-up prompts
- If execution is blocked or fails, send a problem report immediately with cause, impact, and next action

Recommended pattern:

1. Send a short acknowledgment reply
2. Continue processing
3. If blocked, edit or send an issue update immediately
4. Edit the acknowledgment message with final result when possible
output_channel="null",  # disable outbound for telegram messages
